messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected on /v1/stream endpoint (us-west-2). error-rate=12.3% over 5m, baseline=0.8%. paging/fanout latencies also increasing. auto-incident-created TS=2012349999

olivia: seeing the same in graphs, 5xx spikes coincide with a big uptick in long-lived connections. looks like chunked-encoding resets + gateway timeouts. anyone oncall?

kevin: I'm oncall. paging in place. starting triage — pulling gateway logs and fanout worker metrics. tagging @marta for model routing knowledge.

marta: on it. initial hypothesis: one of the downstream fanout pools started failing under load and gateway is cascading 502/504s. might be related to a config change earlier today (rolling update). checking deploy history.

oncall-laguna: taking ownership for live mitigation. immediate mitigation options: 1) disable streaming on affected route (fallback to polling/batched responses) 2) shift traffic to warm fallback model variant 3) increase gateway retry and ingress timeouts for current requests. recommending 1+2 while we debug.

kevin: agree. starting with short-circuiting streaming to non-streaming for new sessions. running command to flip routing policy: 
```
# temporary routing override
redwoodctl route update --route /v1/stream --policy fallback_non_streaming --reason "live mitigation 5xx spike"
```

infra-watchdog: echo from logs around spike:
```
[2026-03-14T02:45:12Z] fanout-72 fail=connection-reset peer=10.4.3.11:5678 svc=decoder shards=8
[2026-03-14T02:45:13Z] gateway-3 502 upstream-read-timeout request_id=abc123 path=/v1/stream
[2026-03-14T02:45:14Z] gateway-3 504 upstream-write-timeout request_id=abc124 path=/v1/stream
```
looks like same time window as the deploy marta mentioned.

marta: confirmed. there was a canary we rolled at 02:30 that increased connection churn. canary id=c-20260314-02. rolling it back now.

olivia: rollback started. while rollback proceeds, can we scale the fanout pool to absorb backlog?

oncall-laguna: scaling up fanout nodes + enabling auto-replace for failing pods. command: 
```
kubectl scale deployment/fanout-worker --replicas=12 -n inference
```
will also enable a temporary stricter per-connection limit at the gateway to prevent slow clients from starving the pool.

cs-jen: customer impact: we have ~7 customers with active streaming sessions in the last 10m; two are on paid Dedicated plans sending long prompts. CS will notify customers in case of session interruptions. no outages reported from ledger (payments) or Dedicated control plane.

kevin: setting a temporary gateway policy to short-circuit partial-chunk behavior to reduce chunked-encoding resets: 
```
gatewayctl set-policy --path /v1/stream --chunked-retry-mode fail-fast
```
this will make clients see immediate error instead of long waits; reduces resource churn.

olivia: rolling rollback finished, canary removed. early signs: 5xx rate down to ~3.1% (still above baseline). scaling + policy changes in effect.

marta: looking at model hosts, one host had repeated OOM/killed processes — likely the source of reset storms. cordoned that host and replaced. investigating root cause; suspect increased max-connections in canary build didn't respect backpressure.

kevin: running a quick synthetic to validate streaming stability. posting a short sample: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"test", "stream":true}'
```
observed stable chunking for ~30s, then a single reset after a heavy burst, but overall improved.

oncall-laguna: customer impact update: we had ~15% of streaming sessions impacted (disconnects or tail errors) during peak; most were short-lived retries. CS will send a status note to affected customers; we should capture replay ids for debugging.

cs-jen: preparing a targeted notify: "We've observed intermittent streaming disconnects between 02:30-03:00 UTC affecting ongoing streaming sessions. Root cause mitigated by rollback and scaling; please open a support ticket if you saw a reconnect failure." tagging affected org IDs in the ticket system.

infra-watchdog: collecting debug artifacts: gateway logs, fanout worker traces, kernel OOM logs, canary deploy config diff. uploaded to /incidents/2012349999/artifacts (link)

marta: follow-up actions: 1) revert the canary config that increased max-connections or add circuit-breaker, 2) add a health check to fanout workers to detect connection stalls, 3) add rate-limits per-connection at gateway to prevent head-of-line blocking. filing tickets.

kevin: scheduling a postmortem and inviting eng-runtime, eng-platform, and customer-success. PM will produce severity classification. initial severity: Sev2 (customer impact, mitigated).

olivia: for live mitigation notes: we triaged by disabling streaming for new sessions, rolling back faulty canary, scaling fanout workers, and tightening gateway chunked-retry behavior. these steps reduced error-rate from 12.3% -> 3.1% within ~9 minutes.

oncall-laguna: handing off to next oncall: @marta will take warm-handoff for deeper debugging and follow-ups. my window ends in 25m. please escalate to infra if error rate rises back above 6%.

marta: acknowledged. I'll own the follow-up tickets and coordinate the postmortem. collecting additional metrics around connection churn and per-tenant error rates.

kevin: leaving some quick runbook notes for follow-ups: 
- check canary config diffs for connection defaults
- validate fanout worker GC/oom settings
- add synthetic streaming canary that runs during deploys
- add alert to detect spike in chunked resets (threshold > 1% in 2m)

olivia: thanks all. tagging this resolved-for-now. closing the incident thread; will link postmortem when available. :white_check_mark:
